You're going to need a few things: a spare inner tube (or a patch kit if you're doing it yourself), a pump with a gauge, and maybe some soapy water for testing leaks. First, deflate the tire completely—don't just take off the valve cap; let all the air out. Then pop the rim strip off to expose the valve core, and screw that thing in tight to seal it up. Next, slide the new tube inside, making sure the edges don't pinch against the rim, then inflate it just enough to give it shape. Finally, mount the tire over the rim, starting at one end and working your way around, being careful not to trap stones or debris between the tube and rim. Once it's seated, remove the valve core (if you're using a direct-mount system) or leave it in if it's standard, inflate to the correct pressure listed on the tire sidewall, and double-check that the bead is fully locked into place.  Pro tip: If your valve has a protective cap, make sure it's removed before taking off the rim strip—some caps are glued shut and can ruin the seal if left on during disassembly.
